methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 5 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in Drones & Autonomous. Range: $800M - $8.6B.

private.name: Joby Aviation
private.rationale: Same sector (Drones & Autonomous), same stage (Public), post-money $6.86B

data.narrative:
Archer Aviation is a publicly traded company in the Drones & Autonomous sector, having raised $1.5B+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of five same-sector comparables across comparable valuation tiers, including both public and late-stage private companies: Wayve ($8.6B, Series D), Zipline ($7.6B, Series G), Joby Aviation ($6.9B, public), Nuro ($6.0B, Series G), and Elroy Air ($800M, Series B).

The peer-median approach, applicable given sufficient comparable transaction activity in autonomous vehicles and drone delivery, yields a median valuation of $6.9B across the five-company set. This method produced an implied valuation range of $800M at the low end (Elroy Air) and $8.6B at the high end (Wayve), reflecting the stage and maturity dispersion inherent in the sector. No additional triangulation methods were applied given single-method availability in the data set.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $5.8B to $7.9B, centered on $6.9B, against Archer's current public market valuation of $3.33B. The gap between current market price and peer median suggests material upside or indicates the market is pricing in execution risk, regulatory uncertainty, or lower near-term revenue visibility relative to the comparables. Key uncertainties include certification timelines for urban air mobility platforms and the sustainability of current private valuations absent demonstrated unit economics.
